text:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple GPU drivers reporting Xid 13/31 resets across cluster region-us-west-2. Affected hosts: gpu-nodex-07, gpu-nodex-09, gpu-nodex-11. Error rate spike at 6031234565. Paging oncall.
oncall-ryan: saw the same in the dashboard — p95 latency for inference up 4x. Is this an ECC burst or driver noise? :eyes:
sre-jane: initial telemetry shows correctable ECC counters increasing + kernel nv-host-reset warnings. GPU memory pressure + container OOMs on the serving runtime on nodex-09.
eng-runtime-lee: logs from one pod:
```
E tensorflow: out of memory allocating KV cache 32768 -> oom
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 13
container: runtime: killed by signal 6
```
support-ana: any customer impact yet? any 5xx spike? I can preemptively open bridge if so.
oncall-ryan: small set of requests returning 502/504s for a few customers hitting nodex-09. I'm opening bridge and tagging affected customers.
incident-bot: BRIDGE OPENED: https://redwood.bridge/6031234567
infra-mark: immediate action: cordon gpu-nodex-09, start drain with --force for runtime pods. Also schedule GPU driver restart on nodex-07/11 if resets continue.
sre-jane: running `kubectl drain gpu-nodex-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` now. Will move serving pods to gpu-nodex-02/04 (cold spare) and fallback routing to cpu-tier for any remaining requests.
eng-runtime-lee: pushing a hotfix to runtime to reduce KV cache preallocation (temporary) and enable conservative batching on the fallback path to avoid OOMs when nodes flake.
oncall-ryan: update: nodex-09 drain completed, most pods rescheduled. nodex-07 still showing Xid chatter at low frequency. nodex-11 had a container restart loop — lost 3 cores worth of capacity briefly.
sre-jane: telemetry snapshot attached (copied):
```
metric: gpu_xid_errors
nodex-07: 12
nodex-09: 34
nodex-11: 27
metric: gpu_ecc_correctable
nodex-07: 430
nodex-09: 1200
```
infra-mark: plan: 1) keep cordon on nodex-09 2) manual driver restart on 07/11 during maintenance window in 10m 3) if Xid persists, roll GPU driver to previous validated build across region.
support-ana: letting affected customers know: limited 502s for small subset, routed to fallback, no data loss, we are mitigating and will follow up. Posting in customer channel now.
eng-runtime-lee: triggered temporary routing policy: route model=redwood-small to dedicated-coldpool and model=redwood-large to cpu-fallback for 15m.
oncall-ryan: doing driver restart on nodex-07 now: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` — monitoring.
incident-bot: Automated runbook suggestion: consider KV cache eviction and reduce max_sequence_length for high-throughput routes.
sre-jane: after restart nodex-07 Xid rate dropped to baseline. nodex-11 still at 0.4x previous, nodex-09 remains cordoned pending hardware ticket.
infra-mark: opened HW ticket with vendor — possible ECC DIMM flapping on nodex-09. RMA queued. ETA 48-72h.
support-ana: posting interim advisory to customers with affected requests, recommending clients retry with backoff. Added note about fallback routing stable.
oncall-ryan: postmortem notes for handoff: - root cause: likely ECC-correctable burst triggering driver resets on nodex-09 leading to OOMs in runtime. - mitigation: cordon+drain, driver restarts, routing fallbacks, runtime kv-cache soft-limit. - action items: schedule hardware diag, add alert on correctable ECC rate crossing 500/min, add auto-evac policy when correctable spikes > threshold.
eng-runtime-lee: will ship runtime config change to enable on-the-fly kv cache trimming (can be toggled per-node) in the next patch; marking CR for triage.
incident-bot: BRIDGE CLOSED: incident stable, follow-ups assigned.
